question: why binary search is log n and not n/2, confused
reference: Each step halves the remaining array (n, n/2, n/4, ... 1), which takes about log2(n) steps, so it is O(log n). n/2 would be the count after only one step.

question: Why is building a heap O(n) and not O(n log n)?
reference: heapify sifts down from the last parent; most nodes are near the bottom and move only a short distance, so the total work is about 2n swaps, i.e. O(n).

question: my recursive fib(45) is super slow, why
reference: Naive recursion recomputes the same subproblems again and again, giving O(2^n) time. Memoization (lru_cache or a dict) makes it O(n).

question: dfs on grid never finishes on big input, what am i missing
reference: Cells are not marked as visited, so DFS revisits them endlessly. Keep a visited set and check it before recursing.

question: In a min-heap where is the smallest element and what does heappop cost?
reference: The smallest element is at the root, index 0. heappop is O(log n) because the last item sifts down at most the height of the tree.
